artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the integer sequence $\{Q_k\}_{k\ge 0}$ by
$$Q_k \;=\; \sum_{j=0}^{k} \binom{k}{j}^{2}\binom{2j}{j}.$$
Let $p$ be an odd prime. Determine whether each of the following congruences modulo $p^2$ holds.

(i) Suppose $p\equiv 1\pmod{8}$ and write $p=x^{2}+2y^{2}$ with $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $x\equiv 1$ or $3\pmod{8}$. Then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{Q_k}{32^{k}}\binom{2k}{k}^{2}\;\equiv\;(-1)^{(p-1)/8}\!\left(4x-\frac{p}{x}\right)\pmod{p^{2}}.$$

(ii) Suppose $p\equiv 1$ or $3\pmod{8}$ and write $p=x^{2}+2y^{2}$ with $x\equiv 1$ or $3\pmod{8}$, and additionally $y\equiv 1$ or $3\pmod{8}$ when $p\equiv 3\pmod{8}$. Then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{k\binom{2k}{k}^{2}}{32^{k}}\,Q_k\;\equiv\;\begin{cases}(-1)^{(p-1)/8}\!\left(\dfrac{p}{x}-2x\right)\pmod{p^{2}}, & \text{if }p\equiv 1\pmod{8},\\[4pt](-1)^{(y+1)/2}\,2y\pmod{p^{2}}, & \text{if }p\equiv 3\pmod{8}.\end{cases}$$

Prove or disprove the two congruences.

While many of Z.-W. Sun's supercongruence conjectures have been resolved by Guo, Zudilin, Mao, and others, no clear evidence was found that this particular pair of congruences has been settled, so the status is recorded as unknown.
